newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares end with gains after tight trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares end with gains after tight trade.

text.p: Greek equities ended with small gains after a late session buying spree pushed the benchmark index 0.23 higher. Trade was tight in moderate turnover boosted by block trades as construction felt selling pressure.
Brokers said the market was hit by a combination of a cash shortage and the negative effect of a law governing investment services, effective November 1.

"Excluding block trades we had moderate trading volume with selling pressure persisting in the construction shares as an imbalance between supply and demand still exists in this sector," said Apostolos Constandinidis, fund manager at Hambros Hellenic Mutual Funds.

"Investment flows seem to prefer the bond market at the expense of stocks right now. We should see strong resistance around 900 points while the market's upside potential right now is rather contained," he said.

The bourse came under selling pressure on Thursday because of the lack of fresh cash injections and concern about the negative side effects of law 2396/96 governing the operation of investment firms in Greece, brokers said.

The chairman of Greece's Capital Markets Commission, Stavros Thomadakis, presented three regulations on Thursday concerning the implementation of law 2396/96 which was voted in parliament last April and goes into effect on November 1.
The law outlines the general framework governing the activities of firms offering investment services in Greece and harmonises Greek law with European Union legislation.
The market was waiting to see how National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou would shape the 1997 draft budget, due by the end of November.
The Athens general share index closed up 0.23 percent, or 2.13 points higher at 929.28 from Thursday's 927.15 close after opening at 926.66 points.
Turnover rose to 10.58 billion drachmas on volume of 5.64 million shares boosted by block trades in Parnassos, and Atemke.

Losers led gainers 137 to 72 with 29 issues unchanged on 238 traded. Banks firmed 0.11 percent, industrials closed 0.50 percent higher but construction tumbled 1.41 percent. Small-caps fell 0.83 percent.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 545-563 at the close. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, ended up 20 drachmas at 4,070.

The Merrill Lynch stock index call warrant based on a basket of 23 shares was quoted at 170.60-179.60 drachmas. It expires on January 9 1998 with a strike price of 1000. It closed in the money at 1015.3.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $9.87-$10.87. The strike price is set at $99.6 and the warrants expire October 8 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted at 4,065-4,310 drachmas at the close. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
